issues.problem:
This sentence is false against the code. Fix A (MassProps.ownership l.386-395) only skips a part q when Shapes.sameSolid(q, H[t]) is true for a part ALREADY in H. Take an exact copy and relabel it into a slot that outranks its original's: Ctrl+D, then the slot through Properties or Ctrl+1-4 (§11.10). The copy then stands above the cleaned parts between the two slots and joins their higher sets, where its original (below them) does not.

Build (work/relabel.luau; every part through Canonical.draft): F2 + hsteer2's sealed Iron box (walls 11-16 0.02 thick, cavity 0.26) + Guard filler 17 (0.258 x 0.258 x 0.23 at (0, 4.1, -0.014)) + Guard filler 18 (0.258 x 0.258 x 0.22 at (0, 4.1, 0.03)) + two Blade Dust Balls 0.02 in wall 16. Its cleaned share is 39,946 of 40,000.
- Ctrl+D of 18, relabelled Blade: the copy outranks 17 and joins 17's higher set.
- Mass 1.288800782 -> +2.3865e-3 kg, balance +4.1979e-3; G the same (0.0928 0.4204 0.1939).
- This is equal to the bit to relabelling 18 itself to Blade (mass 1.2911855317459571 both ways).
- Round 5 = round 4 = f7ac37d. So there is no regression: the behaviour is §4.3's named measuring residual through the slot rank, and fix A's rule ('of one already counted') is right. Only this summarising sentence overstates it.
- Variants: the S0 build moves 0. S3's copy of 18 relabelled Blade moves -3.148e-4 on round 4 and f7ac37d, 0 on round 5.
